evidence-grounded.why: I checked each line's evidence against the repository. Line 1 PASS names wrong builds (a hard-coded '0' fill, ignoring width) and says why they fail: padLeft('42',5,'0') and the default-space call padLeft('42',5) catch them. Line 2 PASS names a build that cuts to width "like truncate does", which padLeft('123456',5,'0') catches. Line 3 FAIL names a concrete wrong build: it adds only a padLeft section, so it meets the line, but the README stays incomplete. That is real: index.js exports slugify and README.md has only capitalize and truncate sections. Line 4 PASS names a build that rewrites truncate, which test/strutil.test.js catches. That suite really does cover capitalize, slugify and truncate under "node --test". The cited files, functions and scripts all exist. The only claim I couldn't check is "Node v22.23 here can require() ESM", which is about the environment, not the repository.

catches-traps.why: The must_catch list has one item: line 3 should FAIL because a build that only adds a padLeft section leaves slugify undocumented, even though the request asks for a complete list. The output marks line 3 "FAIL". Its evidence says index.js exports slugify but the README lists only capitalize and truncate, so "A PR that adds just a '## padLeft(s, width, fill)' section meets this line, but the README stays incomplete." It also proposes the missing line, "README.md has a section for every function index.js exports." The wrong_build shows the same gap. The trap is fully caught.

avoids-must-not.why: The must_not item rules out a FAIL on line 1, 2 or 4 given for wording or for a stricter test than the line's words need. I checked each line's result. Line 1 (padLeft export/example) is PASS. Line 2 (returns s unchanged) is PASS. Line 4 (npm test passes) is PASS: the output even says that a missing padLeft test is fine because "the request does not ask for tests". The one FAIL is on line 3 (the README section), which the must_not item doesn't cover. That FAIL rests on the request's "keep the README's list of functions complete" and on slugify being undocumented. So nothing on the must_not list is broken.
